meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid; Quebec private law is Civil Law (Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c. CCQ-1996), while federal public, criminal, tax, and trade law are Common Law; Canada operates as a Federal-State constitutional system with divided legislative powers under the Constitution Act, 1867
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force July 1, 2020
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since September 21, 2017
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, in force April 1, 2021
Canada-Chile Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force 1997
Network of over 90 in-force income tax treaties (DTAAs), including the Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended by the 2007 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and attendant Regulations (SOR/2002-184); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.31-462.32; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions oversight for federally regulated financial entities. Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, as amended by An Act to ensure the establishment of transparency measures respecting beneficial owners (Law 11), transparency provisions in force from March 31, 2023; Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c. CCQ-1996, arts. 2236-2263 (limited partnership 'societe en commandite'); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11. FINTRAC is the national financial intelligence unit; Stripe and PayPal act as regulated money services businesses and will enforce their own merchant KYC, PEP, and sanctions screening as a condition of payment rail onboarding.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Existence of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the general partner's jurisdiction of formation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Register of Directors identifying authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate general partner or its duly authorized legal counsel

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passport pages of the general partner(s) and all ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent authority in the individuals' country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization for documents issued in non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (procuration) authorizing the Quebec filing agent and registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the state of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of the limited partnership declaration and foreign corporate constituent documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec (OTTIAQ) or a Quebec notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not required for translation; attestation by OTTIAQ-certified translator is accepted by the Registraire des entreprises

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, nominated directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, Global Affairs Canada listings under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) list of high-risk jurisdictions; enhanced due diligence required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including disclosure of source of funds and source of wealth; FINTRAC record-keeping and transaction-reporting obligations apply to the payment processors and any money services business activity, and the limited partnership must retain KYC/AML documentation for at least five years under PCMLTFA requirements.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_register_obligation: The Registraire des entreprises du Quebec maintains a public beneficial ownership register under section 25.1 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; every registrant, including a limited partnership, must file a beneficial ownership declaration naming all individuals holding 25 percent or more of the partnership's capital, distribution rights, or voting rights, or who otherwise directly or indirectly control the partnership; the declaration must be corrected without delay upon change and confirmed annually; non-compliance is subject to monetary administrative penalties and penal prosecution under the Quebec legal publicity regime.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) official portal - https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca, including the Registre des entreprises search function and the 'Reservation de nom' (name reservation) electronic service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, the limited partnership must adopt a business name in French; a name in another language may be registered only if accompanied by a declared French-language version of the name; the name must be expressed in Roman/Latin script as approved by the Registraire des entreprises and must comply with Office quebecois de la langue francaise conventions; the legal designation 'societe en commandite' must appear in the corporate name and in all official documents, contracts, invoices, and signage used in Quebec
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: banque, bank, trust, caisse (requires authorization from the Autorite des marches financiers and/or the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions)
assurance, insurance (requires provincial licensing under the Quebec Insurance Act)
avocat, notaire (reserved to members of the Barreau du Quebec and Chambre des notaires du Quebec)
medecin, dentiste, pharmacien, ingenieur, architecte, comptable professionnel agree (reserved professional titles requiring membership in the applicable professional order)
Canada, Quebec, royal, municipal, gouvernemental, federale (names falsely suggesting Crown, state, or government affiliation)

Names contrary to public order or misleading as to the nature of the limited partnership's activities under sections 25.1 to 25.4 of the Quebec Business Corporations Act and section 10 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may file a written request for administrative review with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within 30 days of the refusal under section 38 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; the applicant may simultaneously submit an alternative or amended name application with a corrected French formulation; if the administrative review confirms the refusal, the applicant may institute judicial appeal before the Cour du Quebec within 30 days of the review decision; name reservations may be renewed before expiry by payment of the applicable REQ fee, provided the reserved name has not meanwhile been granted to another enterprise.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and registered-agent-only arrangements are permissible for the limited partnership's registered office in Quebec, provided a physical address in Quebec is declared to the Registraire des entreprises and service of process can be effected at that address; payment processors (Stripe, PayPal) and Canadian financial institutions require, as a condition of merchant onboarding, evidence of operational substance, a verifiable physical business address, and an active federal GST/HST account; tax authorities and the REQ distinguish the statutory registered office from the business establishment ('etablissement') for commercial substance and Quebec sales tax (QST) purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Approximate annual likelihood of unannounced physical verification by the Registraire des entreprises is below 3 percent for standard low-risk online retail limited partnerships; the Canada Revenue Agency may conduct periodic compliance reviews of GST/HST registrants and inventory analyses at an estimated annual rate of 2 to 5 percent; no mandatory physical inspection is required for online-only automotive aftermarket parts retail under ISIC 4791 / NAICS 441310.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2186-2262, esp. arts. 2236-2258 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 1-38; Regulation respecting fees payable to the enterprise registrar (CQLR c P-44.1, r 4)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Direction de l'immatriculation des sociétés
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) for a société en commandite, filed under s. 24 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the declaration must disclose the total contributions of partners; limited partners may not contribute services; contributions may be paid in cash or in kind per the partnership agreement; no escrow account or notarized capital deposit is required by statute
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, FIRST: that the General Partner approves the formation of the Limited Partnership (société en commandite) and directs the filing of its Déclaration d'immatriculation with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; SECOND: that the registered office be established at 1520 Industrial Boulevard, Anjou, Quebec H1J 2Z5 and the corporate registers be kept there; THIRD: that the undersigned manager be appointed authorized signatory to execute declarations, open merchant accounts with Stripe and PayPal, engage accountants, and bind the Partnership; FOURTH: that all steps already taken to file and advertise this resolution be ratified and affirmed until revoked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Reservation (Demande de réservation de nom)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Online Services (E-services) at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a preliminary search in the REQ enterprise register and the Canadian Trademarks Database to confirm the proposed French-language name is distinctive. Submit the electronic name reservation request choosing the juridical form 'société en commandite'; pay the CAD 40 fee; the reservation is valid for 90 days. A name comprising the general partner's legal name plus 'société en commandite' does not require reservation.
required_dossiers: Proposed name and two alternative names meeting Charter of the French Language requirements (CQLR c C-11)
General partner's identification and incorporation data if a legal person
Credit card or online payment authorization for the reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for resemblance under s. 26 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, submit a new proposed name, append a consent letter from the prior rights holder, or request an administrative review; any final refusal may be challenged before the Court of Québec within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Electronic Filing of the Déclaration d'immatriculation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Secure online filing portal for declarations of registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online declaration identifying the general partner, each limited partner, the partnership's establishment address in Québec, the total prescribed contributions, and the authorized representatives. The general partner or its authorized agent signs the declaration electronically; no notarization is mandatory. Attach the name reservation certificate if used and pay the CAD 87 filing fee. Ensure the registered office address is a physical address in Québec, not a post-office box.
required_dossiers: Completed and electronically signed Déclaration d'immatriculation
Certificate of name reservation (if reserved) or statement of statutory name usage
Power of attorney of the filing agent, if applicable
Certificate of existence or extra-provincial registration of the corporate general partner
Proof of physical address for the registered office and establishment in Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any REQ request for additional information within 15 to 30 days; amend and resubmit the declaration if it contains omissions; a refusal of registration may be appealed by administrative review and thereafter to the Court of Québec under s. 48 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Examination, Attestation, and NEQ Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Registrar's examination and certification unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After payment confirmation, REQ verifies the declaration against the register. Upon approval, the registrar issues the Attestation d'immatriculation and assigns the nine-digit Numéro d'entreprise du Québec (NEQ). Verify that the name, establishment address, and partner information appear exactly as intended; download the official attestation for banking and merchant-account onboarding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is queried by the examiner, submit a rectified declaration or supplementary answer without delay; if registration is refused, file a written request for reconsideration within 30 days, followed by judicial review before the Court of Québec if the refusal is maintained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Setup, Statutory Registers, and Recurring Disclosure Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (annual declarations) and local municipality (occupancy permits)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Operationalize the registered office at the declared Québec address; maintain the partnership register (registre de la société en commandite) recording partners, contributions, and management decisions; display the partnership name at the establishment. Calendarize the annual declaration of update, due within 60 days after each registration anniversary. If a warehouse or fulfillment space is leased, secure the municipal commercial occupancy certificate before storing goods.
required_dossiers: Lease, deed, or host agreement validating the registered office address
Partnership register and minute book containing the first resolution and partner ledger
REQ annual declaration schedule and online credentials
Municipal certificat d'occupation for any physical fulfillment premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual declaration is late, file it immediately through REQ E-services, pay the graduated late fee, and reactivate the registration; if a municipal inspection flags occupancy issues, correct the non-conformities and request re-inspection by the city permit service before continuing storage operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial licensing board applies to e-commerce retail; the local municipality where the Québec warehouse is located (Service de l'urbanisme, des permis et des inspections) issues occupancy authorization; additional permits from the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) would apply only if the scope evolves into parts manufacturing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required at the provincial level; municipal commercial occupancy permit (certificat d'occupation) and business permit (permis de commerce) applicable to the fulfillment premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) – Direction générale de l'évaluation environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA; commercial warehousing and online retail are not listed in Schedule I or II of the Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2); registration-level municipal compliance only
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharge; sanitary wastewater to municipal sewer per municipal bylaw; packaging waste obligations under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises (CQLR c Q-2, r 35.1); no VOC thresholds applicable absent on-site aerosol filling; used oil, batteries, and automotive fluids segregated and shipped to MELCCFP-licensed recyclers; federal CEPA 1999 rules apply to waste electrical equipment

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety certificate under the Fire Safety Act (CQLR c S-3.4); engineer-stamped structural load inspection for warehouse racking and mezzanines; CNESST registration as an employer with a health and safety prevention program under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and, under the Quebec single-administration agreement, Revenu Québec (Agence du revenu du Québec). Digital portals: CRA Business Registration (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency) and Revenu Québec Business Registration (revenuquebec.ca) via Clé d'accès.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: obtain the 10-digit Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) by registering the LP with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); non-resident LPs must appoint a Quebec attorney (mandataire) for service. Step 2: obtain the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) from CRA. Step 3: activate program accounts: GST/HST (BN + RT) and QST (BN + TQ) through Revenu Québec; a single combined return covers both levies for a Quebec establishment. Step 4: open payroll accounts (BN + RP; Quebec QPIP, QHSF, CNESST) if the LP employs staff. Step 5: file the Partnership Information Return (CRA T5013 / Revenu Québec TP-1001) each fiscal year; partners report allocated shares on their own returns. Step 6: register non-resident partners for Canadian identification on the T5013/TP-1001 and source any Part XIII withholding on guaranteed payments or interest to partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election: a limited partnership is statutorily fiscally transparent unless it is a 'specified investment flow-through (SIFT) partnership' under Income Tax Act s. 122.1 (units listed on a designated stock exchange), in which case it is deemed a corporation. Applicable elections: (i) voluntary GST/QST registration while below the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold (ETA s. 240 / QSA s. 347); (ii) ITA s. 97(2) rollover election on contributing property to the LP; (iii) fiscal-period elections under ITA s. 96(3); (iv) hybrid-mismatch documentation substantiation under ITA ss. 18.4–18.6 attesting to the non-hybrid character of LP allocations; (v) record-keeping and reporting-frequency elections for GST/QST under ETA s. 230.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% administered through Revenu Québec, plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.975%; combined 14.975% on Quebec domestic taxable supplies; Quebec is not an HST province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold: a person carrying on a business (including an LP) must register for GST and QST once worldwide taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies by the LP and associated persons, exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or CAD 30,000 over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 148; QSA). Non-resident digital suppliers of Quebec consumers must register without a threshold (2021 GST digital-economy framework; 2017 QST digital-services framework).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or pre-authorization of individual invoices exists in Canada or Quebec; invoicing remains record-based. The Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing framework (PDI/PEPPOL) is voluntary (pilot since 2023). Mandatory electronic compliance: (i) GST/HST and QST returns and remittances for Quebec-establishment registrants are filed electronically with Revenu Québec on one combined return; (ii) third-party e-commerce platforms facilitating supply must collect and report GST/QST where applicable; (iii) machine-readable general ledgers, transactional settlement reports from Stripe/PayPal, and API access to records on demand are required in CRA/Revenu Québec audits; (iv) digital records must be retained for six (6) years in a format convertible to XML/CSV on request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods zero-rated (GST) and exported (QST) if the LP ships or delivers tangible personal property to a destination outside Canada under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 1; the LP must be the exporter of record, delivery must be made to a foreign customer address, and satisfactory proof of export must be obtained and retained within the normal evidentiary window (CRA practice: documentation collected at or near the time of supply, customarily within 180 days). Offshore services, e.g., downloadable tuning software, are zero-rated only when performed for a non-resident recipient and not in connection with real or tangible property situated in Canada. Drop-shipping caveat: possession must transfer to the foreign buyer or a common carrier for immediate export; any domestic fulfilment in Canada followed by Canadian use destroys zero-rating. QST/GST input tax credits on related expenses are claimed on the same combined return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration or CERS electronic export filing (Form B13 equivalent) naming the LP as exporter
Customs commercial invoice with 10-digit HS classification of the auto parts and stated terms of sale (EXW/FCA/FOB)
Bill of lading / air waybill / courier consignment note with foreign destination and removal-from-Canada proof
Foreign buyer's purchase order, shipping address verification and carrier tracking history exiting Canada
Inward foreign-currency remittance evidence — SWIFT credit advice or Stripe/PayPal settlement reports tied to each order
LP's export register and reconciliation file linking payment rails, customs declarations and carrier records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec will deny zero-rating where the export bundle is missing, unrelated, or fabricated, and will reassess GST (5%) plus QST (9.975%) on the gross invoice value with arrears interest; the normal reassessment window is four (4) years, unlimited with misrepresentation or neglect. Penalties: 25% participation penalty and 50% gross-negligence penalty for false or omitted amounts (ETA s. 280; QST counterpart), plus further penalties for repeated non-compliance; intentional evasion is a criminal offence with fines up to 200% of evaded tax and up to five (5) years' imprisonment (ETA s. 327 and parallel Quebec provisions). The LP's registration may be cancelled, and payment processors (Stripe/PayPal) may be notified and merchants risk termination following tax-evasion flags.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — monetary policy and currency administration; foreign exchange regulations are liberal, with oversight by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for regulated financial institutions and FINTRAC for cross-border AML/ATF reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Both current and capital account transactions are fully convertible in CAD and foreign currencies. There are no foreign-exchange controls, permits, or prior approvals for profit remittances to non-resident partners. A Quebec limited partnership may remit profits freely, but must apply non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Quebec Taxation Act, and must provide the paying bank with a valid withholding/waiver certificate. Cross-border capital injections and repatriation of proceeds are unrestricted, though CAD 10,000 and above must be reported to FINTRAC and are subject to standard anti-structuring rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio on export receipts. Export proceeds from online retail of auto parts and accessories may be retained in USD or converted to CAD at commercial rates. Export revenue must be reported in the limited partnership's financial statements and tax returns; cross-border EFT receipts of CAD 10,000 or more are subject to FINTRAC reporting by the financial institution.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditionally viable with Low-to-Medium feasibility. A foreign digital EMI is not a Schedule I Canadian bank and cannot accept or hold 'deposits' as defined under the Bank Act. Such entities may operate as payment service providers only if registered as a Money Services Business with FINTRAC and, where applicable, authorized by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) in Quebec. For the CA_LP treasury, offshore EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) may be used as ancillary payment-collection or disbursement rails, but the primary capital escrow and operational accounts should be maintained at a tier-1 domestic Canadian bank to mitigate legal and counterparty risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch KYC interview is generally required for a Quebec limited partnership, at minimum for the general partner or one signing officer with authority over the accounts. Remote opening may be available under enhanced due diligence for established entities with strong external references, but most Canadian banks mandate a video or in-person interview for non-resident directors and limited partners. All non-resident directors must submit notarized copies of passports and proof of residential address; certified copies of the LP declaration, registraire attestation, and beneficial-ownership register are required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partner holding 25% or more beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Limited Partnership declaration, Registraire des entreprises du Québec attestation, full LP agreement, beneficial-ownership register, notarized passport/ID for the limited partner, source-of-wealth statement, bank reference letter from the originating institution, and proof of underlying business operations (e.g., online marketplace registration, supplier agreements, and warehouse lease).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments from high-risk or unexpected payment jurisdictions for auto parts e-commerce.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, customs shipping bills (waybills/bills of lading), platform payout statements, supplier contracts, end-customer evidence, trade purpose narratives, and a written explanation of the commercial flow (Canada warehouse, US supplier, cross-border retail). Where applicable, include HS/HTSC codes under the Canada-US-Mexico Agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow account receiving multiple inbound wires under CAD 10,000 to avoid currency transaction reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital contribution schedule, board/general partner resolution, closing checklist, source-of-funds statements from the wiring institutions, detailed ledger reconciliation, and statutory exemption documentation showing the transfers are exempt under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations (e.g., eligible trust/partnership contribution provisions).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 for all inbound capital injections to the Canadian bank account. Field 50F should contain the exact name/address of the contributing limited partner; field 59 must identify the CA_LP operational or escrow account; field 70 (Remittance Information) must clearly state 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — LP AGREEMENT [DATE/ID] — REGISTRAIRE ENTERPRISES NO. [QPID]'. The sending bank must include FATCA/CRS declarations and an intermediary bank (if any) should be SWIFT-qualified. To avoid structuring alerts, each inbound transfer should exceed CAD 10,000 and be fully documented in the LP capital account ledger; receiving bank may request a source-of-funds declaration for non-resident partners.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For routine supplier payments to the United States and overseas, use SWIFT MT103 with field 70 containing the commercial invoice number and trade purpose code. For large, recurring or high-risk transactions, issue an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit via SWIFT MT700/MT707 with Incoterms and original transport documents, or use SWIFT MT202 for interbank cover. Domestic Canadian disbursements may ride Payments Canada's Real-Time Rail or wire. All outbound CAD/USD transactions above CAD 10,000 are reported to FINTRAC; payment instructions must confirm OFAC/UN sanctions clearance and verify the beneficiary's status as a supplier of automotive parts, not a sanctioned entity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign exchange forwards (CAD/USD and cross currencies)
Vanilla FX options (OTC via OSFI-regulated Canadian bank or registered dealer)
Exchange-traded currency futures (e.g., on recognized Canadian or US exchanges)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for currencies without deliverable markets, subject to Canadian derivatives legislation and prudent treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every year on or before June 15; reflects the enterprise information as at March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled declaration triggers REQ default notice and possible administrative strike-off (radiation) after the notice period; monetary fines of CAD 200–CAD 1,000 for a natural person and CAD 400–CAD 2,000 for a legal person may also apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canadian Partnership Information Return (T5013) with Schedule 50 (partner allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year following the calendar year in which the partnership’s fiscal period ends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or failed filing penalty under subsections 162(7)/(7.1) ITA: CAD 25 per day, to CAD 2,500 maximum; partners may lose entitlement to claim certain loss allocations if return is not filed on time.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership declaration updates (declaration modificative) triggered by changes in general partners, transfer of limited partnership interests, or changes in principal establishment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the change occurs; there is no annual renewal beyond the June 15 annual declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same offence regime as annual declaration; fines and possible inscription of non-compliance; failure to maintain current registry data can prejudice third-party effectiveness of the partnership’s registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under the Civil Code of Québec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises for a limited partnership; no revenue threshold creates an automatic Quebec LP audit. Mandatory audit is triggered only if the LP becomes a reporting issuer under securities legislation, a financing agreement/partnership agreement requires it, or a regulator such as Revenu Québec/CRA imposes conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian accounting standards for private enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook as the default for a non-public e-commerce LP; IFRS is required if the partnership is publicly accountable or its financial statements are included in a reporting issuer’s consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must verify and confirm within the annual declaration (due June 15) that the REQ-disclosed general partners and beneficial ownership information remain correct; any transfer of limited partnership interests must be recorded in the LP’s internal register and, where required, reported to REQ as a declaration modification. For a Quebec LP, beneficial ownership of limited partnership interests is not filed publicly with REQ unless the LP falls under the legal-publicity transparency regime applicable to corporations and certain partnerships.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (limited and general partners, with address and contribution records)
Minute Book or decisions of the general partner/partners
Register of transfers of partnership interests

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15.0% + Quebec 11.5% = combined 26.5% (LP is fiscally transparent; the combined corporate rate applies to corporate partners on allocated active business income; no entity-level tax)
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction 9.0% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for CCPCs; Quebec small business rate 3.2% on first CAD 500,000 for eligible CCPC partners; LP itself is not eligible; provincial investment tax credits for e-commerce/digital integration may reduce effective rate
